question.text: 'Additional Return' for a Cat III AIF is calculated as:

answer.text: Difference between NAV/AUM and the higher of the Reference Hurdle and High-Water Mark, at year-end

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook computes Additional Return (the amount eligible for incentive fees) as the excess of NAV/AUM at year-end over a threshold that takes the higher of the Reference Hurdle and the High-Water Mark. Using the higher of the two ensures the manager only earns incentives on returns above the more demanding of the two investor-protection benchmarks. The Trap: Total AUM, capital committed, and fund corpus are stock measures, not the excess-return amount the workbook uses to drive incentive fees. Note: The "higher of Reference Hurdle and High-Water Mark" formulation is illustrated in the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B) examples.
